text:
Maya: heads up — ran through the Go sample-app quickstart and found a real onboarding footgun. the README Docker example uses a build ARG and hardcodes the key into the image history. new users following the quickstart accidentally bake secrets into images. snippet in docs/sample-apps/go/README.md currently:
```Dockerfile
# Dockerfile excerpt
ARG REDWOOD_KEY=your_key_here
ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_KEY
COPY . /app
RUN go build -o /app/bin/server ./cmd/server
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]
```
this makes the key present in image layers and shows up in `docker history` — definitely not good. saw two support tickets from customers who used the sample as-is. :grimacing:

Ethan: yikes. thanks for catching. we should never suggest ARG for secrets. propose updating README + sample Dockerfile to use a runtime env var only (no ARG), and show a sec-best-practice using Docker secrets or passing env at `docker run -e` or via compose. also our Go sample's import path is out of date (README uses `github.com/redwood-ai/go-sdk/v1` but actual module is `github.com/redwood-inference/go-client`). that causes build errors for new devs.

Maya: yep both issues. the server example also reads `REDWOOD_KEY` but everywhere else across quickstarts we standardized on `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. mismatch causes a confusing 401 + compile fail for folks.

DevOps Bot: grep results: found `ARG REDWOOD_KEY` in docs/sample-apps/go/Dockerfile and sample-apps/docker/Dockerfile-templates. found `REDWOOD_KEY` in docs/sample-apps/go/README.md and sample-apps/go/cmd/server/main.go. found import `github.com/redwood-ai/go-sdk/v1` in sample-apps/go/go.mod.

Avery: i'll open a PR to replace the Dockerfile + README examples. PR will include:
- remove ARG usage and any ENV assignment from Dockerfiles; demonstrate runtime injection: `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY ...`
- add a note showing Docker secrets / bind-mount of a creds file for advanced users
- update Go module import path to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-client` and update go.mod + sample code to read `REDWOOD_API_KEY`
- change README example snippet to be minimal and safe, e.g.:
```bash
# run locally (do not bake into image)
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(cat ~/.redwood/key)"
docker build -t redwood-go-sample .
docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDWOOD_API_KEY" -p 8080:8080 redwood-go-sample
```
- add a small CI docs-lint that scans Dockerfiles for `ARG REDWOOD_KEY` or `ARG .*KEY` and fails the docs workflow
- add a unit test in sample-apps/go/tests that runs `go build` in a clean env and a smoke test that starts the binary against tests/mock-server and verifies the outbound Authorization header is `Bearer test-key`

Ethan: please also update the quickstart to call out the correct env var name and show the minimal `curl` check to validate the runtime env is set before starting: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" http://localhost:8080/health` — small step but avoids 401s.

Docs Bot: PR #604 planned changes summary: Dockerfile fixes, go.mod update, README edits, docs-lint addition (scripts/lint-docker-secrets.sh), and smoke test. affected files: sample-apps/go/Dockerfile, sample-apps/go/README.md, sample-apps/go/cmd/server/main.go, sample-apps/go/go.mod.

Maya: perfect. can you also add a short blurb in onboarding KB and ping @support when merged? a quick note to set env var instead of baking keys fixed the two tickets.

Avery: yep will ping support. one more thing — add a small CI check in docs flow that runs `docker history` on the built image in preview and fails if it contains the redwood key string. simple grep to catch accidental secrets before merge.

Ethan: +1 on the docker-history check. also add an item to DOCS-95 to audit sample-app Dockerfiles for any other hardcoded creds (helm charts, k8s manifests, compose files).

DevOps Bot: preview build logs: docs-lint.sh found 2 occurrences; PR branch fixed both. smoke test stub passed in ephemeral runner.

Maya: merged at 2494440450. announced to #onboarding and updated KB. thanks everyone — small drift but big security win. :lock: :tada:
